paper.title: Randomized Exploration in Generalized Linear Bandits

unmapped: the learner knows the mean (link) function mu
the learner knows mu_dot_min (minimum derivative of mu in the unit ball around theta_*) and mu_dot_max, used to set a, c_1, c_2 and tau
settings.definition_quote: A stochastic GLM bandit is an online learning problem where the rewards of arms are generated by some underlying GLM. Let $K$ be the number of arms, $x_i \in \realset^d$ be the feature vector of arm $i \in [K]$, and $\theta_\ast \in \realset^d$ be an unknown parameter vector. The reward of arm $i$ in round $t \in [n]$, $Y_{i, t}$, is drawn i.i.d. from a distribution with mean $\mu_i = \mu(x_i\T \theta_\ast)$. We assume that $\eta_{i, t} = Y_{i, t} - \mu_i$ is $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian

bound.expression_latex: \dot{\mu}_{\max} (c_1 + c_2) \left(1 + \frac{2}{0.15 - 1 / n}\right) \sqrt{2 d n \log(2 n / d)} + (\tau + 3) \Delta_{\max}

symbols.tau: number of initial exploration rounds, chosen so that lambda_min(G_tau) >= max{sigma^2 mu_dot_min^-2 (d log(n/d)+2 log n), 1}

conditions: arm 1 is the unique optimal arm
tuning: tau such that lambda_min(G_tau) >= max{sigma^2 mu_dot_min^-2 (d log(n/d) + 2 log n), 1}

source.label: thm:glm-tsl upper bound
source.quote:
The $n$-round regret of \glmtsl is bounded as
\begin{align*}
  R(n)
  \leq {} & \dot{\mu}_{\max} (c_1 + c_2)
  \left(1 + \frac{2}{0.15 - 1 / n}\right) \times {} \\
  & \sqrt{2 d n \log(2 n / d)} + (\tau + 3) \Delta_{\max}\,,
\end{align*}
where
\begin{align*}
  a
  & = c_1 \sqrt{\dot{\mu}_{\max}}\,, \\
  c_1
  & = \sigma \dot{\mu}_{\min}^{-1}
  \sqrt{d \log(n / d) + 2 \log n}\,, \\
  c_2
  & = c_1 \sqrt{2 \dot{\mu}_{\min}^{-1} \, \dot{\mu}_{\max} \log(K n)}\,,
\end{align*}
and the number of exploration rounds $\tau$ satisfies

results.notes: Regret defined as sum_i Delta_i E[N_i(n)], i.e. pseudo-regret. c_2 substituted in terms of c_1. Paper summarizes this as O~(d sqrt(n log K)). Initial exploration length tau enters additively.

symbols.tau: number of initial exploration rounds, chosen so that lambda_min(G_tau) >= max{4 sigma^2 mu_dot_min^-2 (d log(n/d)+2 log n), 8 a^2 mu_dot_min^-2 log n, 1}

conditions: all feature vectors x_i have at most one non-zero entry
arm 1 is the unique optimal arm
tuning: tau such that lambda_min(G_tau) >= max{4 sigma^2 mu_dot_min^-2 (d log(n/d) + 2 log n), 8 a^2 mu_dot_min^-2 log n, 1}
